steps.title: Build a campfire
steps.desc: A cook crafts a Basic Campfire Kit from one Simple Wood, with Flint and Tinder in the bags, and places it. It burns for 15 minutes, and no other campfire can stand within 100 yards.

steps.title: Add your object
steps.desc: From skill 20 in a profession, you place its object by the fire; the others come from other players. Your camp objects share a one-hour cooldown.

steps.title: Sit down for a minute
steps.desc: Anyone sitting or crafting by the fire for a minute gets the buffs of the objects around it. They last an hour, so you can leave once you have them.

howItWorks.questNote: Around level 5, the quest 'The Great Outdoors' has you sit at a campfire, then sends you to a cooking trainer to learn the Basic Campfire; the trainer sells the Simple Wood and the Flint and Tinder. Each profession you know then gets a quest, handed in to its trainer, that teaches its first camp object.

rules.title: Class Buff Stacking Restrictions
rules.text: A camp buff does not stack with the class buff it copies, such as the Fish Bowl with Blessing of Kings: you keep whichever is higher or active.

rules.title: Rested XP Generation Rules
rules.text: Only Leatherworking's Camp Tent, and the Tanning Rack and Sewing Machine that replace it, give rested experience. Sitting by the tent for 30 seconds raises your rested XP up to 5% of a level (1-hour cooldown). It does nothing if you already have 5% or more.

rules.title: Camp Cooking Monster Kill EXP Bonus
rules.text: Most dishes a cook prepares at camp grant +5% bonus experience from monster kills (does not apply to quests) while you remain Well Fed.

rules.title: Faction Alignment on Banners
rules.text: The Tailoring Faction Banner only buffs players of your own faction.

rules.title: Trading vs. Placement Skill Requirements
rules.text: Crafted camp objects can be traded between players freely, but actually placing one around a campfire requires the profession skill shown on the item.

rules.title: Tier Thresholds & Free Reagent Economy
rules.text: Always check a camp feature's tier before counting on free reagents. The Reagent Economy legacy talent specifically targets Tier 1 components.
